HISTORY & PHYSICAL (DETAILED)

Consult Summary:  
50-year-old man with 5-day history of cough, coryza, low-grade feverishness, sore throat, and mild shortness of breath; assessed via telephone—clinical picture most consistent with viral upper respiratory infection/possible early influenza; given safety-net advice and delayed prescription for amoxicillin if no improvement.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Feeling “run-down” with cough and cold symptoms.  
• Onset & course: Began Saturday evening (≈5 days ago) while out for dinner; symptoms persist.  
• Symptom details  
  – Cough: Predominantly dry; slight sputum in mornings.  
  – Nasal congestion/runny nose (“sniffles”).  
  – Sore throat (possible contribution from shouting at football matches); has not inspected throat.  
  – Mild ear dullness—no significant ear pain.  
  – Dyspnoea: Feels “short of breath,” no chest pain.  
  – Subjective fevers/night sweats; no recorded temperature.  
  – GI: One day of mild diarrhoea at illness onset, now resolved; no nausea/vomiting or abdominal pain.  
  – Myalgias/arthralgias: Generalized stiffness in knees/elbows.  
• Exacerbating/relieving factors: None identified.  
• Pertinent negatives: No chest pain, no significant ear pain, no current diarrhoea, appetite reasonable, maintaining oral intake.

Past Medical History:
• Type 2 diabetes mellitus.  
• Hypertension.  
• Overweight/obesity (self-reported “spare tyre”).  

Medications:
• Metformin – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Lisinopril – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Aspirin (intermittent/OTC) – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
Allergies: Denies known drug allergies.

Social History:
• Lives with wife; adult children live separately.  
• Employment: Factory worker manufacturing steel parts.  
• Alcohol: ~9 pints beer/week (4 pints Saturday, remainder Sunday).  
• Tobacco: Occasional smoker; currently using e-cigarette to reduce cigarettes.  
• No illicit drug use mentioned.

Family History:
• Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
• Vitals: Not recorded (telephone consultation).  
• General/ENT/Chest/Abdomen/Neuro/Musculoskeletal: Not examined in person; patient reports symptoms as above.

Investigations:
• None ordered at this time.

Assessment & Plan:

Overall Impression: Likely viral upper respiratory tract infection / influenza-like illness with mild lower respiratory tract involvement; no clear evidence of bacterial pneumonia at present.

DDx Integration (brief):  
1. Viral URTI / Influenza: Compatible with cough, coryza, myalgias, subjective fever, onset over several days.  
2. Early bacterial bronchitis/pneumonia: Less likely (minimal sputum, no chest pain, no objective fever), but considered—delayed antibiotic provided.  
3. COVID-19 (not discussed; no mention of testing)—unable to rule out (transcript silent).

Issue 1 – Acute respiratory illness  
Assessment: 5-day viral-type illness; mild SOB without red-flag features; comorbid diabetes & HTN increase risk for complications.  
Plan:  
• Supportive care: Rest, adequate fluids, regular paracetamol for fever/myalgias.  
• Delayed antibiotic prescription: Amoxicillin 1 tablet three times daily for 5 days—start only if no improvement or worsening after 24–48 hrs.  
• Safety-net advice: Seek urgent medical attention for worsening breathlessness, high fever, pleuritic chest pain, confusion, or inability to maintain hydration.  
• Follow-up: Reassess next week if not improving or sooner if concerns.

Issue 2 – Chronic conditions (Diabetes, Hypertension)  
Assessment: Chronic, stable on current therapy; acute illness may affect glycemic control.  
Plan:  
• Continue metformin and lisinopril.  
• Monitor blood glucose more closely during illness (advised verbally—transcript implies general counsel).  
• Ensure adequate hydration.

Issue 3 – Smoking & Alcohol  
Assessment: Ongoing alcohol intake at upper recommended limits; cutting down smoking with vaping.  
Plan:  
• Encourage continued smoking cessation efforts; offer referral to smoking cessation services at future review.  
• Brief counselling on moderating alcohol to ≤14 units/week.

General plan items:  
• Provide written/printed information sheet on viral URTI self-care and red-flag symptoms.  
• No investigations or in-person exam deemed necessary today given stable presentation via telephone.

Quality checks:
• Missing but expected: No documented vitals or physical exam findings—telephone consult limitation noted.  
• Allergies explicitly asked; patient denies.  
• Medication doses/frequencies not provided.  
• No conflicting information between transcript and (absent) DDx.  
• Transcript quality acceptable; some informal language but intelligible.
